RESULT — PCA on forms of capital, 39 hundred-year slices (capital.csv, BCE 4300–500)

METHOD EXECUTED
Input: capital.csv (39 rows × 12 Z indicators, 100-year steps, zero missing, already z-standardized; decimal=','). PCA on the correlation matrix (columns re-standardized; this also normalizes ZSichel, which has SD 0.538 as given). Sign convention (fixed, disclosed): PC1 anchored so Social Copper&Gold loads positive; PC2 anchored so Economic Axes&Celts loads positive; identical anchors used in all runs. Script: out/pca_capital.py; full console log: out/pca_output.txt.

(a) LOADINGS TABLE (main run) — PC1 = 30.33% variance (eigenvalue 3.639), PC2 = 19.47% (eigenvalue 2.336); cumulative 49.8%. Kaiser: 4 components with eigenvalue > 1 (3.64, 2.34, 1.55, 1.50); PC1/PC2 interpreted per the question.

  variable                        group                         PC1    PC2  rank|PC1|
  ZAxtSchwert  Hatchets & Swords  Symbolic                     +0.570 +0.082     5
  ZDolch       Daggers            Symbolic                     +0.507 +0.113     6
  Zhausgr      House Size         Symbolic                     +0.429 +0.500    10
  ZCU_AU       Copper & Gold      Social                       +0.777 +0.285     1
  Zamber       Amber              Social                       −0.456 +0.679     9
  ZMonument    Monument Count     Social                       +0.390 +0.447    11
  ZHort        Depot              Economic                     +0.648 −0.164     4
  ZSichel      Sickle             Economic                     −0.285 −0.263    12
  ZBeil        Axes & Celts       Economic                     −0.461 +0.719     7
  ZMW          Monument Size      Economic                     +0.461 +0.598     7
  ZKeform      Pottery Form       Cultural                     −0.673 +0.585     3
  Zkeverz      Pottery Decoration Cultural                      +0.729 +0.103     2

PC1 positive pole: Copper&Gold (0.78), Pottery Decoration (0.73), Depot (0.65), Hatchets&Swords (0.57), Daggers (0.51), Monument Size (0.46), House Size (0.43), Monument Count (0.39). PC1 negative pole: Pottery Form (−0.67), Axes&Celts (−0.46), Amber (−0.46), Sickle (−0.29). PC1 is NOT a uniform richness axis — it mixes signs across groups. PC2 positive pole: Axes&Celts (0.72), Amber (0.68), Monument Size (0.60), Pottery Form (0.59), House Size (0.50), Monument Count (0.45); PC2 negative: Sickle (−0.26), Depot (−0.16); near zero: Daggers (0.11), Pottery Decoration (0.10), Hatchets&Swords (0.08), Copper&Gold (0.29).

(b) SYMBOLIC-CAPITAL CHARACTERIZATION (computed, not assumed)
On PC1, all three symbolic components load moderately POSITIVE and occupy mid-range ranks (5th, 6th, 10th of 12): Hatchets&Swords +0.570, Daggers +0.507, House Size +0.429. They covary with Copper&Gold and Pottery Decoration and oppose Pottery Form/Amber/Axes&Celts/Sickle. Symbolic capital thus participates in the PC1 trajectory (which climbs from EN mean −1.74 through SG −1.12, LN +0.33 to OBA +3.09, dipping to YBA +1.85).
On PC2 the symbolic components are UNEVENLY distributed: House Size (+0.50) sits clearly on the positive, monumental/status-aggregation pole (with Axes&Celts, Amber, Monument Size, Pottery Form, Monument Count) versus the subsistence/stored-wealth pole (Sickle, Depot); Daggers (+0.11) and Hatchets&Swords (+0.08) are near zero, i.e., almost orthogonal to PC2.

(c) 39 SLICES ACROSS PC2 BY PERIOD GROUP (mean ± sd, min–max):
EN (4300–3500): −0.70 ± 2.26, range −3.65…+2.01 — dragged by an extreme negative outlier block of the three earliest slices (4300/4200/4100 BCE, PC2 = −3.65); the remaining six EN slices average ≈ +0.53.
MN (3400–3000): +1.80 ± 0.47 (most positive group, max +2.50 at 3200 BCE).
SG (2900–2300): +0.62 ± 0.37.  LN (2200–1700): −0.44 ± 0.50.
OBA (1600–1200): +0.69 ± 1.29 (peaks +2.14 at 1300 BCE).  YBA (1100–500): −1.12 ± 0.65 (most negative group, min −1.67 at 500 BCE).
So PC2 separates MN/SG/OBA (positive) from LN/YBA (negative), with the earliest EN as a strong negative outlier.

(d) SENSITIVITY CHECKS
1) Covariance PCA on as-given Z (ZSichel not re-standardized): loadings essentially identical — Pearson r with main: PC1 = 0.999, PC2 = 0.995; same signs; symbolic values AxtSchwert +0.570, Dolch +0.529, Hausgr +0.431 (PC2 +0.551). ZSichel standardization is immaterial.
2) 37-slice variant (dropping BCE 4300/4200, matching time_series_data.csv coverage): PC1 structure preserved (r = 0.996; EVR 32.45% vs 30.33%; symbolic loadings +0.545/+0.457/+0.336). PC2 moderately altered (r = 0.77; EVR 16.41% vs 19.47%): Monument Count (0.66) and Copper&Gold (0.49) strengthen on PC2, Monument Size weakens (0.14), Pottery Decoration flips (−0.24); but the symbolic pattern is unchanged — House Size positive (+0.51), Daggers (+0.28) and Hatchets&Swords (+0.20) small positive — and the group ordering on PC2 (MN/SG/OBA positive vs YBA negative) is preserved.

(e) EVIDENCE TRAIL (files in out/)
- pca_capital.py (executed script), pca_output.txt (full log: eigenvalues, EVR, loadings, all 39 slice scores, group summaries), loadings_main.csv, loadings_cov_asgiven.csv, loadings_37slices.csv, scores_main.csv.
- Key numbers: eigenvalues [3.639, 2.336, 1.548, 1.500, 0.878, 0.744, …]; EVR [30.33, 19.47, 12.90, 12.50, …]%.

FINAL HYPOTHESIS (grounded strictly in the computed loadings)
In the PCA over hundred-year slices (4300–500 BCE), the symbolic-capital components are characterized by moderate, positive values on PC1 and an asymmetric distribution across PC2. Hatchets&Swords (+0.57), Daggers (+0.51) and House Size (+0.43) load positively but mid-rank on PC1 (30% of variance), rising jointly with Copper&Gold and Pottery Decoration and against Pottery Form, Amber and Axes&Celts as overall capital intensifies toward the Bronze Age. On PC2 (19% of variance), a contrast between monumental/status aggregation (Axes&Celts +0.72, Amber +0.68, Monument Size +0.60, Pottery Form +0.59, House Size +0.50, Monument Count +0.45) and subsistence/stored wealth (Sickle −0.26, Depot −0.16), the three symbolic components diverge: House Size belongs to the positive, monument-like display pole, whereas Daggers (+0.11) and Hatchets&Swords (+0.08) are nearly orthogonal to PC2. Across the 39 slices, PC2 scores cluster by period — Middle Neolithic most positive (mean +1.80), SG (+0.62) and OBA (+0.69) positive, Late Neolithic (−0.44) and Younger Bronze Age (−1.12) negative, with the earliest Early Neolithic slices (4300–4100 BCE) an extreme negative outlier (−3.65) — so house size tracks the monumental axis through time while the weapon components vary independently of it.

LIMITATIONS / UNCERTAINTIES
- PC signs are indeterminate; fixed by the disclosed anchors (Copper&Gold on PC1, Axes&Celts on PC2); any opposite convention simply flips all signs of a component without changing the structure.
- PC2 is the less stable component (37-slice variant r = 0.77), so the PC2 contrast should be read as indicative, especially the exact loadings of Copper&Gold and Monument Size.
- Period-constant repeated rows mean the 39 slices are not fully independent; effective information is closer to the ~37 distinct slice patterns.
- ZSichel is not unit-variance as given; re-standardization (used in the main run) does not change conclusions (sensitivity 1).

payload.workflow: Loaded data/capital.csv (39 x 12 z-standardized indicators, 100-year slices BCE 4300-500, decimal=','); verified zero missingness and exact agreement with time_series_data.csv raw columns at shared 100-year marks (0 mismatches; _inter columns are forward-fills, unused). PCA on the correlation matrix via numpy eigendecomposition of all 12 indicators (ZSichel re-standardized; group/color excluded); deterministic sign anchors (PC1: ZCU_AU>0, PC2: ZBeil>0). Reported eigenvalue spectrum, explained variance, PC1/PC2 loadings and scores per slice. Sensitivity checks: (1) covariance PCA on as-given Z (loadings r=0.999/0.995 vs main), (2) 37-slice variant dropping BCE 4300/4200 (r=0.996 PC1, r=0.77 PC2, symbolic pattern unchanged).
